services.name: Frontend
services.description: Single-page calculator interface and client-side calculation logic.

questions.question: Which language should the frontend use?

options.label: TypeScript
options.description: Adds static typing for safer UI and calculation logic.

options.label: JavaScript
options.description: Uses standard browser JavaScript without a type system.

questions.rationale: TypeScript is a practical default for a maintainable single-page application.

questions.question: Which frontend framework should be used?

options.label: React
options.description: A widely used component-based library with a mature ecosystem.

options.label: Vue
options.description: A progressive framework with approachable component authoring.

options.label: Svelte
options.description: A compiler-based framework with concise components.

options.label: Angular
options.description: A full-featured framework with an integrated application structure.

options.label: Plain HTML/CSS/JavaScript
options.description: A minimal implementation without a frontend framework.

questions.rationale: React is a suitable default for a small interactive calculator and pairs with Fluent UI v9.

questions.question: What calculator capabilities should be included? You can keep the basic recommendation or specify additions such as scientific functions or calculation history.
questions.recommendedChoice: Basic arithmetic (addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division), decimal input, clear/backspace, and keyboard support.
questions.answer: Basic arithmetic (addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division), decimal input, clear/backspace, and keyboard support.
questions.rationale: The request only specifies a calculator, so basic arithmetic is the smallest useful baseline; confirm whether advanced capabilities are important.

questions.question: Which data stores does the application require?

options.label: No datastore required
options.description: All calculator behavior runs in the browser and no data needs to persist.

options.label: PostgreSQL
options.description: Relational storage for persistent application data.

options.label: Blob Storage
options.description: Object storage for files and media.

options.label: Azure Cache for Redis
options.description: Distributed cache for shared, short-lived data.

questions.rationale: The requested calculator can perform calculations entirely in the browser without persistence.

questions.question: Do users need to sign in to use application features?

options.label: Yes
options.description: Users authenticate to access application features.

options.label: No
options.description: The calculator is available without user accounts.

questions.rationale: No sign-in or account-specific behavior was requested.
